pr.title: coverage: Revert "unused local file IDs" due to empty function names
pr.description:
The changes to coverage metadata generation in rust-lang/rust#140847 appear to be the most likely cause of the `function name is empty` errors reported in rust-lang/rust#141577.

If that guess is correct, great. If not, no big deal.

---

This reverts commit 3b22c21dd8c30f499051fe7a758ca0e5d81eb638, reversing changes made to 5f292eea6d63abbd26f1e6e00a0b8cf21d828d7d.

r? ghost
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: This PR is a speculative revert: the description says #140847 is only the “most likely cause” of llvm-cov’s empty function names, adding “If that guess is correct, great. If not, no big deal,” and the supplied evidence does not reproduce or confirm a miscompilation. The concrete changes are coverage-metadata/test-expectation changes: empty covspans are repeatedly left empty in MIR instead of being normalized during InstrumentCoverage, mapping counts/coordinates change, and covfun-record skipping is removed. Those are not ordinary Rust runtime values and cannot ground a program pair whose defined executions differ semantically. The only direct reproducer of the covfun-skipping path was the deleted `unused-local-file.rs` test, which required the test-only `-Zcoverage-options=inject-unused-local-file` flag to manufacture an unused local file ID; without that flag no organic concrete input is established. Constructing a pair that merely compares enlarged-vs-empty coverage coordinates, or an emitted-vs-skipped metadata record, would encode the unconfirmed metadata difference as if it were a confirmed wrong transformation, which the prompt forbids. Therefore no source-grounded original/incorrect function pair with differing defined program values can be validated here.

analysis.originalLogic: After this revert, InstrumentCoverage leaves empty coverage spans in the MIR coverage mappings (for example `21:2: 21:2`) and defers empty-span handling to LLVM codegen's `make_coords`, which calls `ensure_non_empty_span` to grow an empty span over an adjacent `{`/`}` or else drop that mapping. `fill_region_tables` always emits a covfun record for a function and computes counters per mapping, and `Regions::has_no_regions` checks each region table with `is_empty()`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The reverted rust-lang/rust#140847 logic removed by this PR: in `InstrumentCoverage::extract_refined_covspans`, every empty covspan was normalized before merging via `covspans.retain_mut` plus `ensure_non_empty_span`: if the character after the span is `{` it extended hi by one byte, else if the character before is `}` it extended lo by one byte, otherwise the span was discarded. The same commit also added `check_local_file_table`, which scanned `all_cov_spans` and skipped generating the entire covfun record when any local file ID had no mapping region, plus the `inject-unused-local-file` testing option. The description suspects this metadata-generation change caused llvm-cov's "function name is empty" errors.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with coverage instrumentation (`-C instrument-coverage`) containing functions, closures, or async closures with empty coverage spans near brace characters, such as empty bodies or closing braces. The reverted local-file check applies to functions whose local file table contains a file ID with no associated mapping region; the reverted test forced this with `-Zcoverage-options=inject-unused-local-file`. Supplied regression fixtures include `async_closure.rs`, `branch_match_arms.rs`, `instrument_coverage.rs`, and `instrument_coverage_cleanup.rs`.
analysis.summary: Revert of coverage metadata changes that moved empty-span normalization into InstrumentCoverage and skipped covfun records for local file IDs without mappings. The PR description treats #140847 as the likely but unconfirmed cause of llvm-cov "function name is empty" errors; the supplied evidence does not reproduce or confirm the bug. Reusable lesson: empty coverage spans are intentionally representable in MIR and should be handled at coverage codegen, and omitting an entire covfun record for an unused local file ID can remove function metadata.
analysis.trigger: Coverage instrumentation encountering an empty covspan adjacent to `{` or `}`, or a function whose local file table has a file ID with no mapping regions. Under the reverted logic the MIR pass rewrote or discarded the empty span, and/or codegen skipped the function's covfun record entirely.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for the crate/function.
InstrumentCoverage has produced at least one empty coverage span, typically at a brace or empty body.
For the reverted local-file check, a local file ID has no associated mapping region; #140847 used `-Zcoverage-options=inject-unused-local-file` to force this condition.
The reverted #140847 coverage-metadata logic is present rather than the restored pre-#140847 behavior.
pitfalls: Moving `ensure_non_empty_span` from codegen into InstrumentCoverage changes observable MIR span values and mapping counts, e.g. `21:1: 21:2` versus the restored empty `21:2: 21:2`; such test-expectation changes are semantic, not cosmetic.

Skipping the whole covfun record when one local file ID lacks mappings can omit function-name metadata, which is the suspected source of llvm-cov's empty function-name error; this is described only as a likely cause, not confirmed by the supplied patch.

Adjusting a span endpoint by `BytePos(1)` is only valid after checking the adjacent byte is one of the two ASCII brace characters; do not generalize that arithmetic to arbitrary UTF-8 or arbitrary delimiters.
Empty coverage spans are legal in MIR coverage dumps and codegen is expected to cope with them; `all_cov_spans` relies on the invariant that every region contains a span.
Adding or removing the test-only `inject-unused-local-file` option also requires updating `test_unstable_options_tracking_hash`.
analysis.testStrategy: Compile the same Rust source twice with only the empty-span policy changed: baseline leaves empty covspans in MIR for codegen to enlarge or drop, while the historical logic enlarges/discards them during InstrumentCoverage before merging. Compare `InstrumentCoverage` MIR dumps and downstream `CleanupPostBorrowck` dumps, plus cov-map raw bytes and mapping counts. Include empty fn/closure/async-closure bodies and brace-adjacent spans. Separately force an unused local file ID with the inject flag (as in the deleted `tests/coverage/unused-local-file.rs`, using an auxiliary instrumented crate so overall metadata is not empty) and run llvm-cov to assert function names are non-empty. Also test that the `-Z` option set is reflected in the unstable-options tracking hash.
